overall.comments: The 'Not ready to release' verdict and the three next steps are clear: have a developer fix access and sign-out, then tax and quantities, then re-test. Confusing points: 'Behind the screens', 'back-end system', 'Client Portal', 'Admin Portal', 'local demo', 'environment', 'permissions', 'paging', 'screen-reading software' and 'attackers'. I would need someone to get me test logins. The 'Your feedback' fields are not read automatically, so I would not know how to pass on my decisions. The tax example in the headline is a good plain-language lead. There is no mention of who owns the fixes or how long they will take.

detail.title: Customers with large orders are charged too much tax
detail.comments: Steps are simple, but I need a customer test login first, and the report only tells me to ask for one. Step 3 says to 'type a reference' without saying what to type, though any text probably works. The expected figures are clear: $1,050.00 shown versus $1,045.00 correct. I would not know whether 'Client Portal' means the customer website or something else until I tried it. It is clear that customers are overcharged and why that matters.

detail.title: Customers can see other companies' orders
confusing_words: the part that talks to the Client Portal
detail.comments: I understand that one customer can see another company's orders, which is a privacy problem. The location wording is vague to me, and it is not clear how easily order numbers can be guessed. A developer has to confirm it.

detail.title: Customers can read the private records of all customers
confusing_words: the part that talks to the Client Portal
detail.comments: Clear that personal details (phone, ID numbers, addresses, part of card details) are exposed to any customer. Serious, and I understand why. The location wording is jargon.

detail.title: Signing out does not really sign the user out
confusing_words: the part that talks to the Client Portal
detail.comments: I get the gist: after signing out, someone who obtained the old session could still use the account. 'Old sign-in' is a slightly unclear way to describe it, but the shared-computer example helps.

detail.title: The system accepts orders with impossible quantities, even negative ones
confusing_words: the part that talks to the Client Portal
detail.comments: Clear that nonsense quantities such as negative numbers are accepted and distort sales figures. 'Fractional' is a bit technical. Affected people are described as the company's figures and staff, which is fine but I would also wonder about customers.

detail.title: Order search and paging can make the system fail
confusing_words: the part that talks to the Client Portal
detail.comments: I do not understand what 'paging' or 'items per page' means, or how often a person would type a bracket or backslash. It is unclear whether the whole system goes down or just that one search, so I cannot judge how much it matters.

detail.title: A double click or repeated send can create duplicate orders
confusing_words: the part that talks to the Client Portal
sent twice at the same moment
detail.comments: Clear enough: duplicate orders get created. Customers are affected and staff must clean up. It is unclear whether customers are charged twice.

detail.title: Error messages reveal internal technical details
confusing_words: the part that talks to the Client Portal
detail.comments: I do not know what 'broken input' is or what details are revealed, so I cannot tell how bad this is. 'Company's security' is too general to tell me who is actually at risk.

detail.title: On a phone the My orders list is overlapped and totals are cut off
detail.comments: Steps are doable, but I need a test login, and dragging a window edge is not obvious to everyone. A phone is the easier route. The screenshot would help. Customers on phones are clearly affected.

detail.title: Some buttons and fields cannot be understood by screen-reading software
detail.comments: I understand the idea that blind users cannot tell what some controls do. The 'no name' wording is odd, and I would not know how serious this is legally or for the business.

detail.title: The sales report is slow to appear
detail.comments: Simple to follow, with a clear before and after: about four seconds versus a couple. I need an admin test login first. It is clearly minor.

detail.problem: 🔴 Critical: Customers with large orders are charged too much tax
detail.notes: After signing in as QA_ACME1_USER, I filled the New order form with reference PO-TEST-1, Ballpoint Pens box of 50, and quantity 80. After Place order, the message read 'Order PO-TEST-1 placed. Total: $1,050.00.' That matches the report, not the expected $1,045.00. The message didn't show the discount or tax breakdown, so I couldn't check those figures. In step 2 I opened the New order page by its address, because my click on the link failed. The page was the same one the link goes to.

detail.problem: 🟠 Important: On a phone the My orders list is overlapped and totals are cut off
detail.notes: At 375px wide, signing in took me straight to My orders. The first order (PO-4430) is partly hidden behind the Status dropdown and New order button. The Total amounts are cut off at the right edge (for example '$9', '$10', '$8'), and the View link isn't visible without scrolling sideways. I didn't click My orders separately because the sign-in already landed there.

detail.problem: 🟡 Minor: The sales report is slow to appear
detail.notes: After I signed in and clicked Reports, the page showed only the heading 'Sales summary' and a 'Loading' indicator. It was still loading about 5 seconds after my click. The numbers (11 billable orders, $3,008.00 gross sales, orders by status, sales by client) were there a couple of seconds later. I only checked at intervals, so the wait was roughly 5 to 7 seconds, not a precise 4. It was clearly longer than a couple of seconds.
